text: The Patriots head to Jacksonville this Sunday for an AFC showdown with the Jaguars, where they'll need to navigate a defense that's almost certain to deploy Cover-6 coverage—a scheme the offensive game plan will specifically target with "X" plays designed to exploit that look. On the injury front, there's some encouraging news with rookie tight end Eli Raridon returning to practice and being monitored for availability, though the team absorbed a significant blow when initial X-rays confirmed that starting right guard Mike Onwenu has suffered a broken right ankle. The Patriots also made roster moves this week, signing linebacker Jose Ramirez to the 53-man roster from the practice squad while placing safety Dell Pettus on injured reserve and adding linebacker Benton Whitley to the practice squad. Beyond personnel matters, the coaching staff has identified a persistent problem that demands correction before Sunday: after two straight games featuring questionable clock management decisions before halftime, New England must prove it can execute more effectively on possessions late in the second quarter.
